title: Storage Stability: Time, Temperature, Light & Oxygen

content.overview: Storage is an active part of product history. Chemical and sensory attributes can change over time, and the direction or magnitude depends on matrix and exposure conditions.

vocabulary.definition: Measured property capable of showing relevant product change over time.
Contact with oxygen that may contribute to chemical change.
Recorded time and environmental exposure associated with a lot.

sections.title: Time is a process variable
sections.body: Results from different dates cannot be compared responsibly without accounting for elapsed time and storage history.

sections.title: Temperature and light can accelerate change
sections.body: Thermal and light exposure can affect cannabinoid and volatile stability; treatment-specific rates should not be generalized beyond the studied matrix and conditions.

sections.title: Oxygen effects depend on the system
sections.body: Headspace, closure, permeability and opening frequency shape exposure. One packaging claim does not prove preservation of every attribute.

workedExamples: Two retained samples from one lot diverge after different light and temperature histories; the comparison must preserve those histories.
commonMistakes: Comparing old and new results as if storage time were irrelevant.
Treating a cold setpoint as proof of product temperature.
Assuming one protected attribute means total stability.
content.practicalApplication: Build a storage-history table linking lot, package, dates, temperature, light, opening events and stability measurements.
content.summary: Storage conclusions require time- and condition-linked evidence for the attributes that matter.
